tracks.narration: Schedulers usually don't know how long a job will run. MLFQ figures it out by watching what the job does.
Three queues stacked by priority. A new job always starts at the very top. The CPU only runs jobs from the highest non-empty queue.
If a job uses its whole time slice, it must be CPU-bound. MLFQ demotes it to the next queue down. A short job that gives up the CPU stays high.
Without help, a CPU-heavy job could starve forever at the bottom. So every so often, MLFQ lifts every job back to the top queue.
Short interactive jobs stay fast. Long jobs get their fair share. And the scheduler never had to ask how long anything would run.
